conventions.convention: The viewing normal points toward the viewer; (u,v) orients the projection plane positively exactly when (n,u,v) is ambient-positive. A crossing has sign det_P(v_over,v_under). The positive geometric Artin half twist has sign +1.

Total writhe includes mixed crossings; component self-writhe includes only crossings with both branches on that component. Blackboard framing is represented by the positive planar quarter-turn of the projected oriented tangent.
The algorithm accepts finite regular diagrams with declared components, rejects component counts other than two, ignores self-crossings, and returns half the signed mixed sum.

A spanning surface has outward-normal-first boundary orientation. Its positive normal followed by its oriented tangent basis is ambient-positive; negative-to-positive passage contributes +1. A positive meridian bounds an oriented normal disk with positive knot tangent first.
Tubular charts used for framing push-offs must induce the identity from each vertical normal fibre to the ambient normal quotient. Merely fixing the zero section is insufficient.

A framing is a homotopy class through smooth nowhere-zero normal sections. Relative winding needs a supplied reference framing; Seifert framing is defined relative to a supplied surface, without asserting surface existence or zero self-linking here.
The signed-intersection comparison assumes full AC and supplied surface and diagram. The other assigned general invariance and smooth framing claims assume countable choice.
Braid words are traversed bottom to top with the rightmost factor first; closure components are endpoint-permutation cycles.

load_bearing.statement: Crossing sign is the determinant sign of the oriented overpassing and underpassing projected tangents; writhe is their signed sum, and blackboard framing is the positive planar quarter-turn of the projected oriented tangent.

Under countable choice, the mixed crossing sum of a regular oriented two-component link diagram is even; its half is invariant under planar isotopy, all oriented Reidemeister moves, and ambient isotopy. It is symmetric in the components; reversing one component negates it and reversing both preserves it.

Assume AC. For disjoint oriented smooth circles J,K, a supplied compact oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary K transverse to J, and a regular diagram D of their union, the diagram half-sum equals the positive-meridian coefficient of [J] in H1(S3 minus K; Z) and the signed intersection count with the surface. No surface- or diagram-existence theorem is asserted.

Under countable choice, sufficiently small push-offs along a smooth nowhere-zero normal section in a normalized tubular chart are embedded oriented circles disjoint from the knot; their integer linking number is independent of sufficiently small radius, representative in the framing homotopy class, and normalized chart.

Under countable choice, a sufficiently small blackboard push-off in any normalized tubular chart has exactly two mixed projected crossings for each crossing of the original regular knot diagram, both with the original crossing sign, and no other mixed crossings.
Under countable choice, blackboard self-linking equals writhe for a regular knot diagram; componentwise for a link it equals component self-writhe, rather than total link writhe.
